title: AI assistants for small business: choose a tool and finish your first task
summary: Compare ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity by the work you need. See free and paid plan boundaries, complete seller/service/creator examples, and a five-task trial that measures factual errors and correction time.
label: AI assistant buying guide
intro: Choose an assistant by the job, verify the plan and run the same tasks before committing. Includes complete business outputs and a reusable trial kit.

contents.title: Choose the assistant by the job

releaseChecks: The reader can choose a job and identify a plausible assistant route.
Free, individual paid, workspace and API access are clearly distinguished.
Quoted rates specify payment frequency, seat minimums and exclusions.
All three fictional examples contain complete inputs and outputs.
The five-task scorecard has no fabricated observations or quality ratings.
UI instructions are scoped to documented current account interfaces.
Copied data and business promises require an actual factual check.
Internal links lead to the relevant implementation and comparison pages.

priceFacts.scope: Standard seats only; tax, usage credits and other seat types excluded.

currentCapabilityNotes.fact: New GPT creation is unavailable on personal Free, Go, Plus and Pro accounts; managed-workspace permissions differ. This tutorial uses Projects.
Claude standard Projects are available on Free with a five-project maximum; a new Projects beta is rolling out.
A personal paid chat subscription does not establish workspace administration or a separately billed API allowance.

assets.captionBasis: OpenAI-published UI illustration; not a claimed Seller Insider Hub account test.

distinctFromGettingStarted: Buyer intent and tool/plan selection with three industries and a reproducible five-task trial. Existing getting-started guide retains its single bicycle-assessment confirmation workflow.
instructionBasis: Official documentation reviewed. Examples and proposed tests are original editorial material. No firsthand comparative assistant testing, private analytics or business results are published.
